title: Reproducing Goto and Hijikata 2016: SiC growth rates on two faces, and the Si and C emission model as a candidate structure

sample.note: No program reads the off-cut; Song's Si face was on axis.
Figure 3(b) not digitized; 6H, not 4H (“differences … due to the polytype … were within the measurement errors”).

sample.paper: not stated; the analysis model is SiO2 / interface layer / SiC

history.paper: “Oxidation was conducted using an infrared lamp heater”; heat-up rate not stated
history.ours: RUN HeatInArgon DURATION 120 TEMP 25->1200 AMBIENT inert_Ar
history.note: Two minutes is ours. The gas is argon: the optical constants were measured in argon at temperature before oxygen was admitted.

history.paper: “Prior to oxidation, the optical constant of the SiC at the oxidation temperature was measured under an Ar atmosphere.”
history.ours: RUN ArgonAtTemperature DURATION 300 TEMP 1200->1200 AMBIENT inert_Ar
history.note: Five minutes is ours; argon grows nothing in our programs.

history.item: Dry oxygen up to the first read thickness (5.7 nm)
history.paper: “The Ar was then replaced with oxygen and real-time measurements of ellipsometric parameters (Ψ, Δ) were performed.” Figure 3 starts at the first thickness the analysis resolved
history.ours: RUN ToFirstPoint DURATION 437.802 TEMP 1200->1200 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: Figure 3 gives growth rate against thickness, not time. The clock is anchored at the first read point: this step lasts as long as the growth program needs to grow 5.7 nm from its 0.2 nm (7.3 min, from its own constants). That anchor is ours; searched from a quarter to four times it.

history.item: Dry oxygen at 1200 °C, 1 atm, 4.9 h after the first point
history.paper: “at temperatures between 900 and 1200 °C under an oxygen flow of 1000 sccm and oxygen partial pressures from 0.02 to 1.0 atm”; Figure 3 at 1.0 atm
history.ours: RUN Oxidation DURATION 17628.8 TEMP 1200->1200 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: Duration not stated. The times on the curve are integrals of 1/(growth rate) over the read thickness (trapezoid rule), so they inherit the reading error of every earlier rate.

history.paper: “The wavelength range of 310–410 nm was selected for oxide thickness analysis … The angle of incidence was 75.8°. … a three-layer structure was assumed as the analysis model, which consisted of SiO2/interface layer/SiC.”
